name: Zechariah
sourceNote: Translated from the Hebrew of the Westminster Leningrad Codex (the Masoretic Text). It was checked against the Hebrew Minor Prophets scrolls from Qumran (4QXII, 4QXII-a, -e, and -g) and Wadi Murabba‘at (MurXII, early 2nd century AD), whose text is very close to the Masoretic Text. The transcriptions used are Martin Abegg’s, as published in the ETCBC Dead Sea Scrolls dataset. It was also checked against the Septuagint, using Brenton’s public-domain English translation. Portions of Zechariah also survive in the Greek Minor Prophets Scroll from Nahal Hever (8HevXIIgr, about the turn of the era), which is a revision of the Septuagint toward the Hebrew. Its readings could not be checked directly, so any that are cited are marked “reported.” Significant differences are footnoted; differences of spelling and damage to the scrolls are not. The divine title YHWH Tseva’ot is translated “Yahweh of Armies” (see the note at 1:3). Dates are given with their approximate modern months; the notes give the original month and, where it is commonly reckoned, the exact date. Poetry is printed line by line. Verse numbers follow the standard English Bible: English 1:18–21 is Hebrew 2:1–4, and English 2:1–13 is Hebrew 2:5–17.

verses.text: In the eighth month (October–November) of Darius’s second year,{a} Yahweh’s word came to the prophet Zechariah, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, saying,{b}
“Yahweh was very angry with your fathers.
Therefore say to them, Thus says Yahweh of Armies:{c} Return to me, declares Yahweh of Armies, and I will return to you, says Yahweh of Armies.

Do not be like your ancestors, whom the earlier prophets called out to: ‘This is what Yahweh of Armies says: Turn away at once from your wicked paths and your wicked actions.’ But they would not listen or give me any notice, says Yahweh.
Your fathers—where are they? And the prophets—do they live forever?

But the warnings and decrees I commissioned my servants the prophets to deliver, did they not overtake your ancestors? They repented and said, ‘Yahweh of Armies has done to us exactly what he planned for our paths and actions.’”
On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month of Shebat (January–February), in Darius’s second year,{d} Yahweh’s word came to the prophet Zechariah, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, saying,
In the night I had a vision: a man riding a red horse, who halted among the myrtle trees in the glen;{e} behind him were red, chestnut, and white horses.{f}
Then I said, “What are these, my lord?” And the angel who talked with me said to me, “I will show you what these are.”
The man standing among the myrtles replied, “These are the ones Yahweh has sent to patrol the earth.”
They reported to Yahweh’s angel, who stood among the myrtles, “We have patrolled the earth, and look, the whole earth is calm and quiet.”
Then the angel of Yahweh answered, “O Yahweh of Armies, until when will you withhold compassion from Jerusalem and from the cities of Judah, with which you have been indignant now seventy years?”{g}
And Yahweh answered the angel who talked with me with good words, words of comfort.
So the angel who talked with me said to me, “Cry out, saying, ‘Thus says Yahweh of Armies: I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy.
And with great anger I am angry with the nations at ease; for I was only a little angry, but they furthered the evil.
Therefore this is Yahweh’s word: I have come back to Jerusalem in mercy; my house will be rebuilt there, declares Yahweh of Armies, and the surveyor’s cord will be stretched across Jerusalem.’
Proclaim once more: ‘This is what Yahweh of Armies says: My towns will again brim with prosperity, and Yahweh will again console Zion and once more select Jerusalem.’”{h}
And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, four horns!{i}
And I said to the angel who talked with me, “What are these?” And he said to me, “These are the horns that have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.”
Then Yahweh showed me four craftsmen.

I asked, “What have these come to do?” He replied, “These are the horns that dispersed Judah so that nobody could lift up his head. But these craftsmen have come to frighten them and to hurl down the horns of the nations that raised a horn against Judah’s land in order to scatter its people.”

notes.text: Hebrew “in the eighth month,” that is, Marcheshvan (later Heshvan), in the calendar whose year begins in the spring, in 520 BC. No day is given. Because the Hebrew months were lunar, each corresponds to parts of two modern months.
Zechariah means “Yahweh remembers”; Berechiah, “Yahweh blesses”; Iddo perhaps “timely.” Ezra 5:1 and 6:14 call Zechariah “the son of Iddo,” that is, his grandson or descendant. Compare Matthew 23:35.

Hebrew YHWH Tseva’ot, traditionally “the LORD of hosts.” The “armies” are the forces of heaven (the angels and the stars) and sometimes the armies of Israel. The title is translated “Yahweh of Armies” throughout.
Shebat (Shevat) is the eleventh month. As commonly reckoned, this was about February 15, 519 BC.
Or “in the deep place.” The Septuagint has “between the shady mountains” (also in verses 10–11), reading harim, “mountains,” for hadassim, “myrtles.”
The color of the second group (Hebrew seruqqim) is uncertain: perhaps “sorrel,” “bay,” or “speckled.” The Septuagint has four colors: “red, and grey, and piebald, and white.”
Compare Jeremiah 25:11–12 and 29:10. From the destruction of the temple in 586 BC to this vision is about seventy years (counted inclusively).
Hebrew tov, “good,” also “prosperity.”
English 1:18–21 is Hebrew 2:1–4.

verses.text: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, a man with a measuring line in his hand!{a}
I asked, “Where are you headed?” He told me, “To measure Jerusalem, to find out its width and its length.”
And behold, the angel who talked with me went out, and another angel went out to meet him
and he said to him, “Run, speak to this young man, saying, ‘Jerusalem will be settled like unwalled villages, because of the great number of men and cattle in her midst.
And I myself will be to her a wall of fire all around, declares Yahweh, and I will be the glory in her midst.’”
Up! Up! Flee from the land of the north, declares Yahweh, for I have spread you out like the four winds of the heavens, declares Yahweh.{b}
Up, O Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon.
For this is what Yahweh of Armies says: after glory he sent me{c} against the nations that plundered you—for whoever touches you touches the apple of his eye:{d}
“For see, I am swinging my hand over them, and they shall be spoil to their own servants; and you will know that Yahweh of Armies has sent me.
Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion, for behold, I come, and I will dwell in your midst, declares Yahweh.
And many nations shall join themselves to Yahweh in that day and shall be my people. And I will dwell in your midst, and you shall know that Yahweh of Armies has sent me to you.
And Yahweh will take possession of Judah as his portion in the holy land,{e} and will again choose Jerusalem.
Be silent, all flesh, before Yahweh, for he has roused himself from his holy dwelling.”

notes.text: English 2:1–13 is Hebrew 2:5–17.
The Septuagint has “for I will gather you from the four winds of heaven.”
The Hebrew of this phrase is obscure. It may mean “after the glory (that is, the vision) he sent me,” or “with glory he sent me,” or “for his glory’s sake.”

Hebrew “his eye.” Jewish tradition lists this as one of the “corrections of the scribes” (tiqqune sopherim), and it reports that the original reading was “my eye.” The word translated “pupil” (bavah) is literally “gate” or “little one” of the eye.
This is the only place in the Hebrew Bible where the land is called “the holy land.”

verses.text: Then he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of Yahweh, and the Accuser{a} standing at his right hand to accuse him.
And Yahweh said to the Accuser, “Yahweh rebuke you, O Accuser!{b} Yahweh who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Is not this a brand plucked from the fire?”
Now Joshua was clothed in filthy garments, and he was standing before the angel.

And he spoke up and said to those standing in front of him, “Take the filthy clothes off him.” And to him he said, “See, I have made your iniquity pass away from you, and I will clothe you in fine robes.”
And I said, “Let them put a clean turban on his head.” So they put a clean turban on his head and clothed him with garments. And the angel of Yahweh was standing by.
And the angel of Yahweh solemnly charged Joshua, saying,

“This is what Yahweh of Armies says: If you follow my paths and observe my requirements, then you will govern my house and guard my courtyards, and I will grant you free passage among these attendants.
Listen, Joshua the high priest, you and your colleagues seated before you, for they are men who serve as a sign: I am about to bring my servant, the Branch.{c}

For behold, the stone that I have set before Joshua: on one stone are seven eyes.{d} Behold, I will engrave its inscription, declares Yahweh of Armies, and I will remove the iniquity of this land in a single day.
In that day, declares Yahweh of Armies, you shall call each man to his neighbor, beneath the vine and beneath the fig tree.”

notes.text: Hebrew hassatan, “the adversary” or “the accuser.” With the article, it is a title (compare Job 1–2), not yet a personal name. The verb “to accuse him” (lesitno) comes from the same root. The Septuagint has “the Devil.”
Compare Jude 9. The Septuagint has “The Lord rebuke you, O Devil.”
Hebrew tsemah, “sprout” or “shoot,” a title of the coming king from David’s line (Jeremiah 23:5 and 33:15). See also 6:12.
Or “seven facets.” The verb translated “engrave” is used for cutting gems; the Septuagint has “I am digging a trench.”

verses.text: Then the angel who had spoken to me before came back and woke me, like someone woken from sleep.

And he said to me, “What do you see?” And I said, “I have looked, and there is a lampstand entirely of gold, and its bowl upon its top, and its seven lamps upon it, seven and seven pipes for the lamps that are upon its top.{a}
And there are two olive trees by it, one on the right of the bowl and the other on its left.”
And I answered and said to the angel who talked with me, “What are these, my lord?”
Then the angel who talked with me answered and said to me, “Do you not know what these are?” I said, “No, my lord.”
Then he answered and said to me, “This is the word of Yahweh to Zerubbabel: Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, says Yahweh of Armies.
What are you, great mountain? In front of Zerubbabel you will become level ground. He will bring out the capstone to shouts of ‘Blessing, blessing on it!’”{b}
Moreover, the word of Yahweh came to me, saying,
“Zerubbabel’s hands have laid this house’s foundation; his hands will also finish it. Then you will recognize that Yahweh of Armies sent me to you.

For who has despised the day of small things? For these seven shall rejoice and shall see the plumb stone in the hand of Zerubbabel.{c} These are the eyes of Yahweh, which range through the whole earth.”
Then I answered and said to him, “What are these two olive trees on the right and the left of the lampstand?”
A second time I asked him, “What are the two olive branches next to the two golden spouts that empty out the golden oil?”{d}
He answered me, “Do you not know what these things are?” And I said, “No, my lord.”
Then he said, “These are the two sons of oil{e} who stand by the Lord of all the earth.”{f}

notes.text: That is, perhaps seven pipes to each lamp (forty-nine in all), or fourteen in all. The Septuagint has “and seven oil funnels to the lamps.”
Or “Beauty, beauty to it!” (Hebrew hen hen). The Septuagint differs: “I will bring out the stone of the inheritance, the grace of it the equal of my grace.”

Hebrew “the stone, the tin” (ha’even habbedil), probably a plumb weight or a separating stone. The Septuagint has “the plummet of tin.” In the Hebrew, “these seven” are the eyes of Yahweh (compare 3:9).
The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. The word translated “pipes” is unique, and the last phrase is literally “that empty the gold out of themselves.”
Hebrew bene hayyitshar, “sons of fresh oil,” that is, the anointed ones. They are probably Zerubbabel and Joshua. Compare Revelation 11:4.
Hebrew adon, “lord,” not the divine title Adonai. This title also appears at 6:5.

verses.text: Again I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, a flying scroll!{a}
And he said to me, “What do you see?” I answered, “I see a flying scroll. Its length is thirty feet, and its breadth fifteen feet.”{b}

He told me, “This is the curse sweeping over the surface of the whole land. Everyone who steals will be removed, as the one side of the scroll declares, and everyone who swears falsely will be removed, as the other side declares.{c}

I will send it out, declares Yahweh of Armies, and it shall enter the house of the thief and the house of him who swears falsely by my name. And it shall lodge in the midst of his house and consume it, both its timber and its stones.”
Then the angel who was speaking with me stepped forward and told me, “Look up and notice what is appearing.”
And I said, “What is it?” He said, “This is the measuring basket that is going out.”{d} And he said, “This is their eye in all the land.”{e}
And behold, a round cover of lead was lifted,{f} and this was a woman sitting in the basket!
And he said, “This is Wickedness.” And he cast her down into the middle of the basket, and cast the lead weight upon its opening.
Then I raised my eyes and looked, and there came out two women, with wind in their wings; and they had wings like a stork’s wings, and they raised the basket up between the earth and the heavens.
Then I said to the angel who talked with me, “Where are they taking the basket?”
He said to me, “To build a house for it in the land of Shinar.{g} And when it is prepared, it will be set down there on its base.”

notes.text: The Septuagint has “a flying sickle,” reading maggal for megillah.
Hebrew “twenty cubits … ten cubits,” about 9 by 4.5 meters. A cubit is about 18 inches (45 centimeters).
Or “shall be cleaned out” or “shall go unpunished.” The Hebrew word (niqqah) is ambiguous. Each side of the scroll apparently bore one of the two curses.

Hebrew ephah, a dry measure of about 3/5 bushel (22 liters). Here it is the container that held that amount, a basket or barrel; so also in verses 7–11. It could not normally hold a person, which marks this as a vision.
Hebrew “their eye.” The Septuagint has “their iniquity,” reading ‘awonam for ‘enam, a difference of one letter. Many translators follow it.
Hebrew kikkar, “round thing,” the same word used for a talent, a weight of about 75 pounds (34 kilograms). Literally “a talent of lead”; the Septuagint has the same.
Shinar is Babylonia (Genesis 10:10 and 11:2, the land of the tower of Babel). The Septuagint has “the land of Babylon.”

verses.text: And again I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, four chariots coming out from between two mountains! And the mountains were mountains of bronze.
With the first chariot were red horses, and with the second chariot black horses,
in the third chariot white horses, and in the fourth chariot spotted, strong horses.{a}
Then I answered and said to the angel who talked with me, “What are these, my lord?”
The angel replied, “These are heading out to the four winds of heaven, after standing in the presence of the Lord of the whole earth.{b}
The one with the black horses is going out to the land of the north, and the white have gone out after them,{c} and the dappled have gone out to the land of the south.”
And the strong ones went out and sought to go and walk to and fro through the earth. And he said, “Go, walk to and fro through the earth.” So they walked to and fro through the earth.
Then he called to me and said, “Look, those heading to the northern land have settled my Spirit in the northern land.”{d}
And the word of Yahweh came to me, saying,
“Take from the captivity, from Heldai, from Tobijah, and from Jedaiah, and come yourself on that same day; come to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, where they have arrived from Babylon.{e}
Take from them silver and gold, and make crowns,{f} and set it on the head of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
And speak to him, saying, ‘Thus says Yahweh of Armies: See, a man whose name is Branch! From his place he shall sprout up,{g} and he shall build the temple of Yahweh.
He is the one who will construct Yahweh’s temple and wear majesty, and sit and govern from his throne. There will also be a priest at his throne,{h} and the two will share a peaceful understanding.’
And the crown shall be for Helem and for Tobijah and for Jedaiah and for Hen son of Zephaniah, as a memorial in the temple of Yahweh.{i}
People from far away will come and help build Yahweh’s temple. Then you will recognize that Yahweh of Armies sent me to you. All this will happen if you faithfully listen to Yahweh your God.”

notes.text: The colors are uncertain. The Hebrew of the fourth group has two words (“dappled” and “strong”); the Septuagint has “piebald and ash-coloured.” In verse 7, “strong” (amutstsim) may be another color.
Or “These are the four spirits of heaven.” The Hebrew ruhot means both “winds” and “spirits.”
Or “toward the west” (literally “behind them”). The Hebrew does not mention a group going east.
Or “have set my anger at rest.” The Hebrew is literally “have caused my spirit to rest.” The Septuagint has “my anger.”

Heldai means “mole” or “enduring”; Tobijah, “Yahweh is good”; Jedaiah, “Yahweh knows”; Josiah, “Yahweh supports.” The Septuagint translates the names as common nouns: “from the chief men, and from the useful men of it, and from them that have understood it.”
Hebrew ‘atarot is plural (“crowns”), but the verb “set” and the verb in verse 14 are singular. It may mean a single elaborate crown.
Hebrew yitsmah, “he shall sprout,” a play on Tsemah, “Branch.” Compare 3:8.
The Septuagint has “and there shall be a priest on his right hand.”

Helem is probably Heldai (verse 10), and Hen (“grace”) is probably Josiah. Hen may also be translated “as a kindness to the son of Zephaniah.” The Septuagint has “to them that wait patiently … and for the favour of the son of Sophonias, and for a psalm in the house of the Lord.”

verses.text: In King Darius’s fourth year, Yahweh’s word came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, Kislev (November–December).{a}
Now Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and their men to entreat the favor of Yahweh,{b}
saying to the priests of the house of Yahweh of Armies and to the prophets, “Shall I weep in the fifth month (in July–August), abstaining as I have done these many years?”{c}
Then the word of Yahweh of Armies came to me, saying,

“Speak to everyone in the land and to the priests: In the fifth and seventh months (September–October) of these seventy years, when you fasted and mourned, was it really for me that you fasted, for me?{d}
And when you eat and when you drink, is it not you who eat and you who drink?
Were not these the words that Yahweh proclaimed by the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, with her cities around her, and the Negev and the lowland were inhabited?”{e}
And the word of Yahweh came to Zechariah, saying,
“Thus says Yahweh of Armies: Judge with true justice; show steadfast love and compassion, each to his brother;
do not exploit the widow, the orphan, the foreigner, or the poor; and let none of you plan harm against a fellow Israelite in your heart.”
But they would not pay attention; they turned a stubborn back and dulled their ears so they could not listen.
They made their hearts like adamant so as not to hear the law and the words that Yahweh of Armies had sent by his Spirit through the former prophets. Therefore great wrath came from Yahweh of Armies.
“And it came to pass that as he called and they would not hear, so they called and I would not hear,” says Yahweh of Armies,

“and I scattered them with a storm wind among all the nations that they had not known. Thus the land was left desolate behind them, so that no one went to and fro, and they made the pleasant land a desolation.”

notes.text: Kislev (Chislev) is the ninth month. As commonly reckoned, this was about December 7, 518 BC, nearly two years after the visions of 1:7–6:15.

Or “Now Bethel-sharezer had sent Regem-melech and his men.” Sharezer means “protect the king”; Regem-melech perhaps “friend of the king.” The Septuagint has “And Sarasar and Arbeseer the king and his men sent to Bethel.”

Hebrew “in the fifth month,” that is, Ab. The fast in this month mourned the burning of the temple in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:8–9). The Septuagint has “The holy offering has come in here in the fifth month.”
Hebrew “in the fifth and in the seventh,” that is, Ab and Tishri. The fast in the seventh month mourned the murder of Gedaliah (2 Kings 25:25).
Hebrew Negev, “the dry country,” the south of Judah; and the Shephelah, “the lowland,” the low hills toward the coast.

verses.text: And the word of Yahweh of Armies came, saying,
“Thus says Yahweh of Armies: I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and I am jealous for her with great wrath.
Thus says Yahweh: I have returned to Zion and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem, and Jerusalem shall be called the City of Faithfulness, and the mountain of Yahweh of Armies, the Holy Mountain.
Thus says Yahweh of Armies: Old men and old women will yet dwell in the broad places of Jerusalem, each man with his staff in his hand for very age.
And the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing in its streets.
Thus says Yahweh of Armies: If it is too wonderful in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, should it also be too wonderful in my eyes? declares Yahweh of Armies.
Thus says Yahweh of Armies: Behold, I will save my people from the land of the sunrise and from the land of the sunset,{a}
and I will bring them to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. And they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in faithfulness and in righteousness.”

Thus says Yahweh of Armies: “Let your hands be strong, you who hear in these days these words from the mouth of the prophets, which were spoken in the day the house of Yahweh of Armies was founded, that the temple might be built.
For before those days there were no wages for people or for animals; and nobody who traveled was safe from the enemy; I set everyone against his own neighbor.
But now I will not deal with the remnant of this people as in the former days, declares Yahweh of Armies.
For peace will be sown: the vine will yield its fruit, the soil will give its harvest, and the skies will release their dew. I will let the remnant of this people inherit all of this.{b}
And as you have been a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, so will I save you, and you shall be a blessing. Do not fear, but let your hands be strong.”
For this is what Yahweh of Armies says: “Just as I resolved to bring calamity on you when your ancestors made me furious, and I did not change my mind, says Yahweh of Armies,
so in these days I have turned and purposed to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Fear not.
These are the things you are to do: Speak truth each man with his neighbor; judge with truth and with a judgment of peace in your gates.
Do not scheme harm against your neighbor in your heart, and do not delight in perjury; for I hate all of these things, declares Yahweh.”
And the word of Yahweh of Armies came to me, saying,

“This is what Yahweh of Armies says: The fasts of the fourth month (June–July), the fifth, the seventh, and the tenth (December–January) will become happy and joyful holidays for Judah’s house, times of cheerful celebration.{c} So cherish truth and peace.
“Thus says Yahweh of Armies: Peoples shall yet come, even the inhabitants of many cities.
And the inhabitants of one will go to another, saying, ‘Let us go promptly to seek the favor of Yahweh, and to seek Yahweh of Armies. I too will go.’
Many peoples and strong nations shall come to seek Yahweh of Armies in Jerusalem and to entreat the favor of Yahweh.

Thus says Yahweh of Armies: In those days it shall be that ten men out of all the languages of the nations shall grasp, yes, grasp the corner of the garment of a man who is a Jew,{d} saying, ‘We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.’”

notes.text: Literally “from the land of the rising and from the land of the going in of the sun,” that is, from east and west.
Or “For there shall be the seed of peace.” The Septuagint has “But I will show peace.”

Hebrew “the fast of the fourth, … the fifth, … the seventh, and … the tenth” months. The fourth month (Tammuz) mourned the breach of Jerusalem’s wall (Jeremiah 39:2); the fifth (Ab), the temple’s burning; the seventh (Tishri), Gedaliah’s murder; and the tenth (Tebeth, December–January), the beginning of the siege (2 Kings 25:1). See 7:3, 7:5.
Hebrew kanaph, the “corner” or “hem” of a garment, where tassels were worn (Numbers 15:38).

verses.text:
and Hamath also, which borders on it,
Tyre and Sidon, though they are very wise.

Look, the Lord will dispossess her
and hurl her might into the sea,
and fire will consume her.

Ashkelon will see and be afraid,
and Gaza, and she will tremble greatly,
and Ekron, for her hope is put to shame.
A king will perish from Gaza,
and Ashkelon will not be lived in;

a mixed people shall dwell in Ashdod,{d}
and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.

And I will camp around my house as a garrison,
against any who pass through and return;
no taskmaster will pass through them again,
for now I have seen with my eyes.

As for you, because of the blood that sealed your covenant,
I will release your captives from the dry cistern.

Return to the stronghold, O prisoners of hope;
today also I declare that I will restore to you double.

How good he is, and how lovely!
Grain will make the young men thrive,
and fresh wine the young women.

notes.text: Hebrew massa’, “burden” or “oracle.” Chapters 9–11 and 12–14 begin with the same heading, and Malachi 1:1 does too.
Or “for Yahweh has an eye on mankind.” The Hebrew is difficult. The Septuagint has “for the Lord looks upon men, and upon all the tribes of Israel.” Hadrach was a region in Syria.
Hebrew matsor, “stronghold,” is a play on Tsor, “Tyre.”
Hebrew mamzer, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps “people of mixed birth” or “foreigners.” It appears elsewhere only in Deuteronomy 23:2.
Or “like a chief” (Hebrew ’alluph). The Septuagint has “a captain of a thousand.”
Hebrew nosha‘, literally “saved” or “delivered,” perhaps meaning “victorious.” The Septuagint has “saving.” “Humble” (‘ani) also means “afflicted” or “poor”; the Septuagint has “meek.”

Quoted in Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15. Hebrew poetry often repeats an idea in two parallel lines (here, “on a donkey, on a colt”). Matthew’s account mentions both a donkey and a colt (Matthew 21:2–7).
Compare Psalm 72:8. “The River” is the Euphrates.
Hebrew Yavan, Ionia, that is, the Greeks. The Septuagint has “the Greeks.”
Hebrew shophar. Here the divine name is Adonai YHWH, translated “the Lord Yahweh.”
Or “they shall devour and trample on the sling stones.” The Hebrew is difficult. The Septuagint differs.
The Hebrew is uncertain, and the verb may mean “sparkle” or “be raised like a banner.” The Septuagint has “for holy stones are rolled upon his land.”

verses.text:
Ask of Yahweh rain
in the time of the latter rain;
Yahweh makes the lightning flashes,
and he gives them rain in showers,
to each man grass in the field.

And they will be like warriors,
trampling in the mire of the streets in war;
and they will fight, for Yahweh is with them,
and the riders of horses will be put to shame.

And I will bring them back from the land of Egypt,
and from Assyria I will gather them;
and to the land of Gilead and Lebanon I will bring them,
and room will not be found for them.

He will cross the sea of trouble,
and beat down the sea’s waves,
and the Nile’s depths will all run dry;
Assyria’s arrogance will be humbled,
and Egypt’s scepter will vanish.

I will make them strong in Yahweh,
and they shall walk in his name,”{c} declares Yahweh.

notes.text: Hebrew teraphim, household idols used in divination (compare Genesis 31:19 and Ezekiel 21:21).
Hebrew ‘attudim, “male goats,” that is, the leaders of the flock.
A Qumran Minor Prophets scroll (4QXII-g) reads “they shall glory in his name,” and the Septuagint is similar (“they shall boast in his name”).

verses.text:
Open your doors, O Lebanon,
that the fire may devour your cedars!

Howl, O cypress, for the cedar is fallen,
because the majestic ones are laid waste!
Howl, O oaks of Bashan,
for the forest that could not be entered has come down!{a}

Hark, the howling of the shepherds,
for their splendor is laid waste!
Hark, the roaring of young lions,
for the pride of the Jordan is laid waste!{b}
Thus said Yahweh my God: “Shepherd the flock doomed to slaughter.
Their buyers butcher them and go unpunished, and their sellers declare, ‘Praise Yahweh, I am rich!’ and their own shepherds show them no compassion.

For I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land, declares Yahweh. But see, I am handing the men over, each one into his neighbor’s hand and into his king’s hand; and they shall beat the land to pieces, and from their hand I will not rescue.”
So I shepherded the flock doomed to slaughter, truly the afflicted of the flock.{c} And I took two staffs; one I named Favor, and the other I named Union.{d} And I shepherded the flock.
And I made away with the three shepherds in one month.{e} And my soul was short with them, and their soul also abhorred me.
Then I said, “I will not feed you. The dying, let it die; and the perishing, let it perish; and those that remain, let them eat each one the flesh of her fellow.”
Then I took my staff called Favor and snapped it in two, canceling the covenant I had made with all the nations.
So it was annulled on that day, and the afflicted of the flock, who were watching me, knew that it was the word of Yahweh.
And I said to them, “If it is good in your eyes, give my hire; and if not, refrain.” And they weighed my hire, thirty pieces of silver (about 12 ounces).{f}
And Yahweh said to me, “Cast it to the potter—the splendid price at which I was valued by them!” And I took the thirty pieces of silver and cast them to the potter in the house of Yahweh.{g}
Then I broke my second staff, even Union, so as to break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
And Yahweh said to me, “Take for yourself again the gear of a foolish shepherd.

For see, I am raising up a shepherd in the land; the perishing he will not visit, the young he will not seek, the broken he will not heal, the one standing he will not sustain; but the flesh of the fat he will eat, and he will tear off their hoofs.

Woe to the worthless shepherd,
who forsakes the flock!
A sword upon his arm
and upon his right eye!
His arm shall wither away completely,
and his right eye shall be dimmed completely!”

notes.text: Hebrew (Qere) “the inaccessible forest” or “the forest of the vintage” (Kethiv). The Hebrew is uncertain.
Hebrew ge’on hayyarden, “the pride of the Jordan,” that is, the thick growth along its banks (Jeremiah 12:5).

Or, with a slightly different division of the Hebrew letters, “for the sheep merchants” (likena‘ane hatstso’n); so also in verse 11. The Septuagint has “in the land of Canaan” here, and in verse 11 “the Canaanites.”
Hebrew No‘am, “Favor” or “Pleasantness,” and Hovelim, “Union” or “Binders.” The Septuagint has “Beauty” and “Line.”
Who the three shepherds were is unknown. There have been many suggestions.

Hebrew “thirty of silver,” that is, thirty shekels. A shekel is about 0.4 ounce (11.5 grams), so the total is about 12 ounces (345 grams). This was the compensation for a slave gored by an ox (Exodus 21:32). Compare Matthew 26:15 and 27:3–10. Matthew 27:9 attributes the prophecy to Jeremiah; it combines this passage with themes from Jeremiah (18:2–3, 19:1–13, and 32:6–15).

Hebrew yotser, “potter.” The Syriac version reportedly has “treasury” (’otsar), a difference of one letter. Compare Matthew 27:6–7. The Septuagint has “Drop them into the furnace … and cast them into the furnace in the house of the Lord.” The phrase “the lordly price” is sarcastic.

verses.text: The burden of the word of Yahweh concerning Israel. The declaration of Yahweh, who spreads out the heavens and lays the foundation of the earth and shapes the spirit of man in his inward parts:
“See, I am making Jerusalem a bowl of reeling to all the peoples round about; and upon Judah also it will be, in the siege against Jerusalem.{a}
And in that day I will make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all the peoples; all who lift it will be badly gashed; and all the nations of the earth will be gathered together against her.

On that day, declares Yahweh, I will afflict every horse with panic and its rider with insanity; but I will keep my eyes open over Judah’s house, while I strike all the nations’ horses with blindness.
And the chiefs of Judah will say in their heart, ‘The inhabitants of Jerusalem are a strength to me in Yahweh of Armies their God.’

“In that day I will make the chiefs of Judah like a firepot among pieces of wood, and like a torch of fire among sheaves; and they will consume, on the right hand and on the left, all the peoples round about; and Jerusalem will yet dwell in her own place, in Jerusalem.
“Yahweh will rescue the tents of Judah first, so that the glory of David’s house and of Jerusalem’s residents will not exceed Judah’s.
On that day Yahweh will defend those living in Jerusalem; the weakest among them on that day will be as strong as David, and David’s house will be like God, like Yahweh’s angel leading them.
And on that day I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

“I will pour out on David’s house and on Jerusalem’s residents a spirit of grace and pleading; they will look at me, whom they stabbed;{b} they will mourn for him as people mourn for an only child, and weep bitterly for him as people weep for a firstborn.
In that day the lamentation in Jerusalem will be great, like the lamentation of Hadad-rimmon in the valley of Megiddon.{c}
And the land will lament, clan by clan apart: the clan of the house of David apart, and their women apart; the clan of the house of Nathan apart, and their women apart;
the clan of the house of Levi apart, and their women apart; the clan of the Shimeites apart, and their women apart;
all the clans that remain, clan by clan apart, and their women apart.

notes.text: Or “And Judah also will be in the siege against Jerusalem.” The Hebrew is difficult.
Some Hebrew manuscripts reportedly read “to him whom they have pierced,” as John 19:37 quotes it (compare Revelation 1:7). The Septuagint has “they shall look upon me, because they have mocked me.”

Hadad-rimmon may be a place near Megiddo, or the name of a storm god (Hadad, also called Rimmon) whose mourning rites were well known. Some connect it with the national mourning for King Josiah, who was killed at Megiddo (2 Chronicles 35:22–25). The Septuagint has “the pomegranate grove cut down in the plain.”

verses.text: “On that day a fountain will be opened to David’s house and to Jerusalem’s residents, to cleanse them from sin and defilement.{a}

“And it will be in that day, declares Yahweh of Armies, that I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they will no more be remembered; and the prophets also and the unclean spirit I will make pass out of the land.

And it will be, if a man prophesies again, that his father and his mother who gave him birth will say to him, ‘You will not live, for you have spoken falsehood in the name of Yahweh’; and his father and his mother who gave him birth will run him through when he prophesies.
And it will be in that day that the prophets will be ashamed, each one of his vision when he prophesies; and they will not wear a mantle of hair in order to lie.
He will say, ‘I am no prophet; I am a farmer, because I have been someone’s servant since I was young.’{b}
And one will say to him, ‘What are these wounds between your hands?’{c} And he will say, ‘Those with which I was struck at the house of those who love me.’

“O sword, wake up against my shepherd,
against the man who is my associate,”
declares Yahweh of Armies.
“Strike the shepherd, and the flock will scatter;{d}
and I will bring back my hand upon the little ones.

Throughout the whole land, declares Yahweh,
two thirds will be struck down and die,
and one third will survive.

That third I will pass through the fire,
refine them the way silver is refined,
and assay them the way gold is assayed.
They will invoke my name, and I will respond;
I will say, ‘They are my people,’
and they will say, ‘Yahweh is our God.’”

notes.text: Hebrew “for sin and for impurity.” The second word (niddah) is used for ritual impurity.
Or “for the land has been my possession since my youth” (reading a different word division). The Hebrew is difficult. The Septuagint has “for a man brought me up thus from my youth.”
Hebrew “between your hands,” that is, on the chest or back. Such wounds were self-inflicted in ecstatic rites (1 Kings 18:28).
Quoted in Matthew 26:31 and Mark 14:27. The Septuagint has “smite the shepherds, and draw out the sheep” (Codex Alexandrinus: “the shepherd”).

verses.text: See, a day is coming that belongs to Yahweh, and your spoil will be shared out in your midst.

And I will gather all the nations to Jerusalem for war; and the city will be captured, and the houses looted, and the women violated; and half the city will go forth into captivity, but the remainder of the people will not be cut off from the city.
Then Yahweh will go out and fight against those nations as when he fights on a day of battle.

And his feet will stand in that day upon the Mount of Olives, which faces Jerusalem on the east; and the Mount of Olives will be split through its middle toward the east and toward the west into a very great valley; and half of the mountain will withdraw northward and half of it southward.

You will run to my mountain valley, for the valley between the mountains will extend to Azal.{a} You will run just as you ran from the earthquake in the time of Uzziah, king of Judah.{b} Then Yahweh my God will arrive, with all his holy ones.{c}
On that day there shall be no light, cold, or frost.{d}
It will be a one-of-a-kind day, known only to Yahweh, neither daytime nor nighttime, yet when evening comes there will be light.
On that day fresh water will flow out of Jerusalem, some toward the eastern sea and some toward the western sea; it will flow in both summer and winter.{e}
And Yahweh will be king over all the earth. On that day Yahweh will be one and his name one.{f}

All the land will be changed into a level plain like the Arabah, from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem; and she will be raised high and will dwell in her place, from the Gate of Benjamin to the site of the First Gate, as far as the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel as far as the king’s winepresses.
And they will dwell in her, and there will no more be a ban of destruction;{g} and Jerusalem will dwell securely.

And this will be the plague with which Yahweh will strike all the peoples who have warred against Jerusalem: he will make their flesh waste away while they stand on their feet, and their eyes will waste away in their holes, and their tongue will waste away in their mouth.
And it will be in that day that a great confusion from Yahweh will be among them; and they will grasp each man the hand of his neighbor, and his hand will rise up against his neighbor’s hand.
And Judah also will fight in Jerusalem; and the riches of all the nations round about will be gathered: gold and silver and clothing in very great quantity.
And so will be the plague of the horse, the mule, the camel, and the donkey, and every beast that is in those camps: like this plague.
And it will be that every one left of all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year by year to bow down to the King, Yahweh of Armies, and to celebrate the Feast of Booths.
And if any of the families of the earth do not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, Yahweh of Armies, there will be no rain on them.
And if the clan of Egypt does not go up and does not come, then not upon them;{h} there will be the plague with which Yahweh strikes the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Booths.
This will be the penalty of Egypt, and the penalty of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Booths.
On that day the horses’ bells will carry the inscription “Holy to Yahweh.” The cooking pots in Yahweh’s house will be as sacred as the bowls in front of the altar.

And every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah will be holy to Yahweh of Armies; and all who sacrifice will come and take from them and cook in them. And there will no longer be a trader{i} in the house of Yahweh of Armies in that day.

notes.text: Azal (or Azel) is an unknown place. The Septuagint has “And the valley of my mountains shall be closed up … and shall be blocked up,” reading nistam (“shall be stopped up”) for nastem (“you shall flee”).
Compare Amos 1:1. The earthquake was in the eighth century BC.
Hebrew “with you.” The Septuagint, the Latin Vulgate, and other ancient versions have “with him.”
Or “there shall be no light; the glorious ones shall congeal.” The Hebrew is difficult. The Septuagint has “there shall be no light, and … cold and frost.”
The eastern sea is the Dead Sea; the western sea is the Mediterranean.
Compare Deuteronomy 6:4 (the Shema): “Hear, O Israel: Yahweh our God, Yahweh is one.”
Hebrew herem, the ban that devoted something to destruction.
The Hebrew is abrupt; the sense is probably “then no rain shall fall on them.” The Septuagint omits “not” and reads “then upon them shall be the overthrow.”
Hebrew kena‘ani, “Canaanite,” also “merchant” (compare Proverbs 31:24).
